chk.verdict: Not ok, but close. Checks 2, 4 and 6 hold. Check 5 holds for sections: L was added and nothing else was removed, though a few K sentences were removed rather than updated (listed below). Checks 1 and 3 each fail on a few sentences. The numbers I found correct: every cache-replay rate and count in section L and its exact-numbers table; the hit rates on the changing questions; the gap-chart values; the 58,125, 161,515 and 185,388 token figures with their prices; the 323-file hub; the 134 dependency cases split 133 and 1, with file-level stale answers by kind (1,191, 101, 123, 123, 38, 35, 21, 0); every feasibility count, against feasibility/NOTES.md; and every cost bar, the 4.0 to 10.0 billion total, the 10 % reserve and the 7 to 11 sessions, 8 to 15 owner hours and 25 to 80 container hours, against protocol-v2.md section 9. In result.json, diffed against the pre-correction backup in page/work3, no numeric leaf changed. The only removed keys are token_bound.*, carried 1:1 into token_estimate. Seventeen text fields changed. index.html is 485,290 bytes. check.js.txt prints "PASSED: no problems". The section list is scope and A to K, now plus L. The scope banner and the first "What it does not show" item of L both say that no model was called, no agent ran, and model-made conclusions were not cached. What fails: three page sentences say more than the evidence (the audit called "independent ... with its own code"; fact-level rules called "safe"; and the K caching row giving the 87.6 % and 6.5 % rates with no qualifier), and two count statements do not match the source (the "seven rules" and "asked again at each of 190 saved versions").

defects.where: graph-test/index.html, section L, 'What it shows', first bullet (data.json l.shows[0])
defects.what: 'An independent audit recomputed all 40,880 lookups with its own code and found 0 disagreements.' The audit wrote only its own loader, driver and reconstruction of what was served. It used the finished test's own SQL programs for kinds 1 to 8, and for completion it ran the same reference code as the replay. The sentence therefore implies an item on the must-not-claim lists in AUDIT.md section 10 and build-h cache.audit: 'The audit verified the question programs' meaning independently'.
defects.fix: Use: 'An audit recomputed the true answer at all 40,880 lookups with its own loader and its own reconstruction of what each rule served, using the finished test's original SQL programs and reference code, and found 0 disagreements. A mistake shared with those programs, about what a question means, would not show.'

defects.where: section K, row 'caching concepts and invalidation', column 'Measured here' (data.json k.rows)
defects.what: '350 questions were asked again at each of 190 saved versions of the code graph under seven rules'. Two things are wrong. The replay ran 11 policies (data.json l.setup.rules = 11; NOTES section 2.5); seven is only the number the chart draws. And not every question was asked at every version: there were 40,880 warm lookups, not 350 x 189 = 66,150, because a question is looked up only where its anchor exists. The same row then gives '87.6 % of lookups ... file level served 6.5 % of its answers stale' with neither qualifier that AUDIT.md section 10 requires: 47.6 % of lookups are of questions that never change, and the 6.5 % rises to 13.2 % on the changing questions.
defects.fix: Use: '...350 questions were looked up again at each later saved version where what they ask about existed (40,880 lookups over 189 steps), under 11 rules. The fact-level rule with the "nothing else" patterns served 87.6 % of lookups (82.5 % on the 112 questions whose answer changes) with no stale answer against the extractor's facts. File level served 6.5 % of its answers stale (13.2 % on the changing questions; the share depends on the question mix).'

defects.where: section L, 'What was done, in plain words'
defects.what: '350 questions about the code were asked again at each of 190 saved versions'. Questions were looked up only at versions where their anchor existed (or had existed at the previous version), which gives 40,880 lookups. The first version has no lookup to check. Read literally, the sentence overstates the schedule.
defects.fix: Use: '350 questions about the code were looked up again at each later saved version where the code they ask about existed (40,880 lookups at 189 versions after the first; there are 190 saved versions in all)...'

defects.where: section L, 'What it shows', sixth bullet (l.shows[5])
defects.what: 'The share served by every safe rule falls as the gap between lookups grows'. Calling the fact-level rules 'safe' leans toward the must-not claim 'Fact-level invalidation is proven safe'. The 'What it does not show' list on the same page denies exactly that.
defects.fix: Use: 'The share served by both fact-level rules (which served no wrong answer in these lanes) falls as the gap between lookups grows (main-chain lanes, not re-checked by the audit).'

defects.where: section K, row 'caching concepts and invalidation', column 'Not measured' (this sentence was on the page before)
defects.what: 'so a cache that only stops repeat reads within one session would save little'. It treats a measured exposure (0.5 to 1.5 % of a window is content fetched a second time) as a saving. That conflicts with widen/result.json refuter 'exposures ..., not savings' and with 'caching does not help'.
defects.fix: Use: '...so a cache that only stops repeat reads within one session acts on at most about 0.5 to 1.5 % of a window (an exposure, not a measured saving).'

defects.where: section K, caching rows (check 5: text that was on the page before section L was added)
defects.what: Three things were removed, not carried into the updated rows. (a) The sentence 'A database cache that keeps unneeded content out of the window would therefore cut cached and uncached tokens alike; how much is untested.' (b) The source '(protocol-v2.md)' after the prompt-cache sentence. (c) The measured note 'The facts cost no model tokens and rebuild in about 5.3 s per commit'. Removing (a) may be intended, since it leans toward 'caching saves tokens'. The removal is not stated anywhere.
defects.fix: Put back '(protocol-v2.md)' and the 5.3 s rebuild figure, for example: 'The facts themselves cost no model tokens and rebuild in about 5.3 s per commit.' Either drop (a) deliberately and say so in the record, or put it back with 'how much is untested' kept.
